question: How much of the money buying AI chips was lent, guaranteed or invested by the companies selling them?

call.stance: The seller finances part of the demand
call.line: Nvidia's receivables ran 9% to 16% of sales above its own collection pace by July 26, 2026; five accounts owed 70% of them.
actions: Compute days outstanding yourself on November 18: receivables over the quarter's revenue, times 91. July 26, 2026 gave 59.6.
Split Nvidia's $108.5 billion of guarantees by when they bind: $105 billion for SB Energy phases in from fiscal 2029; $3.5 billion is live.
Read Broadcom's $29B backstop and the $42B note facility in its Aug 2 10-Q, which Reuters ties to Anthropic, before its Dec 9 report.
flips: Nvidia's 10-Q for the quarter to Oct 25, 2026 puts days outstanding below 51.1, the average before July: the second quarter was a peak.
Free cash flow tops 71% of net income on Nov 18, its average in the four quarters before July: the cash came in and the terms were timing.
AMD or Broadcom reports a gigawatt-scale accelerator deal with no warrant, investment, loan or guarantee by Dec 9: demand pays its own way.

nextTest.event: Nvidia reports its quarter to October 25, 2026: whether days sales outstanding, receivables over revenue times 91, hold at or above 51.1, the average before July, after 59.6 in the quarter to July 26.

resolver.rule: DeepStack computes days sales outstanding from two figures the 10-Q prints: accounts receivable, net on the condensed consolidated balance sheet at October 25, 2026, and revenue on the condensed consolidated statement of income for the three months then ended, times the 91 days of the quarter, rounded to one decimal. The answer is yes if the figure is 51.1 days or more; no if it is below 51.1. The line is the average of the four quarters before the quarter ended July 26, 2026, computed the same way: 54.1 (July 27, 2025), 53.3 (October 26, 2025), 51.4 (January 25, 2026) and 45.4 (April 26, 2026); the quarter ended July 26, 2026 gave 59.6. The payment terms the filing describes are read alongside and do not decide the test.
resolver.question: In NVIDIA's Form 10-Q for its fiscal quarter ended October 25, 2026, is accounts receivable, net at quarter end, divided by the quarter's revenue and multiplied by 91, at or above 51.1 days?

source.label: SEC EDGAR, NVIDIA Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 25, 2026 (balance sheet and statement of income), CIK 0001045810

resolver.ambiguity: If the 10-Q is not public on EDGAR by December 15, 2026, the test is inconclusive, and the Result says what was read and what was missing; the next reading is December 31, 2026. If the period the 10-Q covers is not 91 days, the rule uses the number of days its period dates give. Figures are read as first filed; a later amendment does not reopen the test.

notes.label: The thread
notes.text: Part 1 called Nvidia's demand real and its financing fragile; Part 11 found the longer terms. Part 16 measures where the risk went.

settles.event: Nvidia reports its quarter to October 25, 2026: whether days sales outstanding, receivables over revenue times 91, hold at or above 51.1, the average before July, after 59.6 in the quarter to July 26.
Nvidia reports: whether the guarantees note in its 10-Q puts total maximum exposure above $108.5 billion, the figure in the table for July 26, 2026.
Nvidia reports: whether its 10-Q puts AI cloud agreements, cloud services it commits to buy from its own customers, above the $36 billion of July 26, 2026.
Nvidia reports: whether the direct customers listed at 10% or more of receivables hold more than 70% together, after five held 70% on July 26, 2026.
Anthropic's first public registration statement: its first audited revenue, and how much of it runs through investors that also sell it compute.

lead.name: Clark Tang
lead.line: Third-party money from Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR was underwritten independently and replaces Nvidia's balance sheet rather than stretching it.

lead.name: Daniel Nishball
lead.line: Nvidia acts as a central bank for AI, supplying credit where private lenders will not, because small buyers can pay for GPUs but cannot show a lender a credit rating.

lead.name: Gaetano
lead.line: Customers outside the traditional hyperscalers, from neoclouds to sovereign clouds, produced 59% of Nvidia's data center growth in the quarter to July 26, 2026.

against.name: Kakashii
against.line: Nvidia, acting as supplier, investor, financier and broker, introduced Nebius to four customers worth more than $1 billion each in the first quarter.
against.why: This side says outside capital is taking the seller's place. Kakashii's case is that at Nebius the seller still found the customers and carried the credit.

lead.name: Michael Burry
lead.line: Nvidia's revenue growth is mostly, not wholly, real, because circular financing holds marginal demand for compute above market rates.

lead.name: Kakashii
lead.line: CoreWeave exists mainly to create demand for Nvidia's GPUs: Nvidia is its only GPU supplier and also an investor, customer and sponsor.

lead.name: Distillate Capital Partners LLC
lead.line: Hyperscalers and Nvidia committed about $180 billion to OpenAI and Anthropic, which pledged about $1.1 trillion of compute spending back.

against.name: Longriver
against.line: Anthropic's reported run-rate went from about $1 billion at the end of 2024 to almost $50 billion in May 2026, a sign that customers pay for agentic work.
against.why: This side reads the seller's money as the demand. Longriver's reply is that end customers pay, though its figure is an unaudited run-rate and the labs count revenue on different bases.

lead.name: Ed Elson
lead.line: OpenAI and Anthropic supplied an estimated 60% to 80% of the AI revenue at Amazon, Google and Microsoft and, citing The Information, about half of the hyperscalers' revenue backlog.

lead.name: Mia Silverio
lead.line: Two customers supplied nearly a quarter of Anthropic's 2025 revenue and 47% of its sales ran through Amazon and Google, a concentration a company seeking a $2 trillion value cannot afford.

lead.name: Daniel Romero
lead.line: The two labs' combined run-rate reached $105 billion in July 2026, $65 billion of it Anthropic's, nowhere near what the buildout modeled for 2027 requires.

against.name: Market Sentiment
against.line: The labs priced their newest models at $10 and $50 per million tokens, the band their earlier flagships held at launch, a sign that the leading models keep their pricing.
against.why: This side says the chain rests on two labs that may not earn their keep. Market Sentiment's case is that the labs still hold their prices at the top of the market.

expansions.expansion: Annualized recurring revenue: a month's or a quarter's revenue scaled to a year, not audited revenue.
